answer: Each agent claims one meadow plot with an 80-credit bond, marked by an opal beacon, and files a radar return measuring vine canopy. A gauge records runoff, and an auditor recomputes water use from returns against the gauge level; a mismatch burns the bond. The first plot costs 38 credits, and the kth costs 38 plus 9 times k minus 1, as later plots grow remoter, so 1,000 fake plots cost 4,533,500 in fees plus 80,000 locked. A rented-sensor ring fails because each return is keyed to plot coordinates and beacon signature, so reuse burns both bonds. An honest agent pays once.
